Senses.Explanation: The graph names a buddha and, with the article, the Buddha. It occurs 116,053 times in 459 allowlisted texts, but the Chan record gives this extremely broad title a sharply observable deployment of its own. The Buddha in the lineage-opening scenes is a participant in public actions: the World-Honored One mounts the seat, Kashyapa announces that the Buddha has finished speaking, and the Buddha leaves the seat; at Vulture Peak he holds up a flower before the silent assembly and Kashyapa smiles. The same bare word is made the object of the stock public question "What is Buddha?" (如何是佛), to which the records preserve mutually different answers rather than a common descriptive biography: Yunmen says "a dry shit-stick" (乾屎橛), Dongshan says "three catties of hemp" (麻三斤), and Huangbo says "this very mind is buddha; no-mind is the Way" (即心是佛。無心是道。). Linji supplies an explicit formula in answer to "What are the true buddha, true teaching, and true Way?": "buddha is the mind's purity; the teaching is the mind's brightness; the Way is unobstructed pure light everywhere" (佛者，心清淨是；法者，心光明是；道者，處處無礙淨光是), then calls all three empty names without real existence (三即一，皆是空名，而無寔有). The corpus also turns against the title itself. Zhaozhou's recorded saying is "the one word 'buddha'—I do not like to hear it" (佛之一字，吾不喜聞). A lamp record attributes to Deshan a longer roster beginning "here there is no buddha and no patriarch" (這裏佛也無，祖也無) and ending "buddha is an old barbarian's shit-stick" (佛是老胡屎橛). Linji places buddha first in a five-part roster of whatever one meets inside or outside: "meet a buddha, kill the buddha; meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch; meet an arhat, kill the arhat; meet parents, kill parents; meet kin, kill kin" (逢佛殺佛、逢祖殺祖、逢羅漢殺羅漢、逢父母殺父母、逢親眷殺親眷). Later comments keep the lineage-opening scene open to appraisal: Dongshan Shouchu says people know only the flower and smile but do not know the World-Honored One, while Yulin calls the flower and smile the single transmission of the treasury of the true teaching eye and says it has made clear-eyed people laugh ever since. This is where Chan bends the word: its Buddha is recorded through the flower and teaching-seat actions, answers and self-formulas in public exchanges, refusal and abuse of the title, later appraisal of the lineage-opening scene, and the title's place in a killing roster—not through an outside religious life story.
Senses.Note: This sense covers the figure/title and the word as deployed in Chan, not the physical image separated below. Longer compounds keep their own articles and should not be silently substituted for it: buddha-nature; the question 'What is Buddha?' (如何是佛); 'this very mind is buddha' (即心是佛); 'meet a buddha, kill the buddha' (逢佛殺佛); and denouncing buddhas and reviling patriarchs. The graph in 'the Buddha's teaching' is a compound constituent and does not justify leaving the entire compound untranslated. The curated evidence spans an early lamp compilation, Linji's own record, and Huangbo's record; later compilations and commentaries repeatedly preserve and comment on the same scenes and formulas.

Senses.Explanation: The same bare graph can name a physical buddha image rather than a person or title. The Record of the Chan Gate's Forged Reflections lists the twenty-fifth case as “Danxia burns a buddha” (丹霞燒佛). Wanfeng Zhishan preserves the full material scene: in severe cold Danxia takes a wooden buddha to burn, the monastery chief asks, “Why burn my buddha?” (何得燒我佛), and Danxia stirs the ashes saying, “I am burning it to obtain relics” (吾燒取舍利). An independent record names the same case with the material object explicit: “Danxia burns a wooden buddha” (丹霞燒木佛). Yulin Tongxiu also preserves the material contrast: a gold buddha does not pass through the furnace, a wooden buddha does not pass through fire, a clay buddha does not pass through water, and the true buddha sits within (金佛不度爐木佛不度火泥佛不度水真佛內裡坐). The bare shortened title and the monastery chief's bare “my buddha” therefore identify a physical image, a different object from the buddha addressed, questioned, rejected, or invoked in the primary sense.
Senses.Note: Two exact bare-word anchors establish the image sense: the shortened case title and the monastery chief's question inside the full cold-weather and relic exchange. The independent expanded case name and Yulin Tongxiu's gold, wood, clay, and true-buddha roster are family evidence; neither is allowed to buy bare-headword depth. The longer compound 'wooden buddha' (木佛) remains a related entry rather than replacing this bare-word sense.
